release_notes.en-US: First release. Passive PHP patch-level check: reads the PHP version a server advertises, compares it with the fixed releases for CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619 and the latest release per branch, and warns with a badge, popup, one-line notification and an in-page dialog. Per-site snoozing. Optional single HEAD re-check of the current page (switchable).

version.approval_notes: Passive security extension. It observes response headers with webRequest (read-only, non-blocking) and page hints, and never modifies, blocks or probes anything. The only request it can send to a site is a single HEAD request for the page the user is already on, and only when no version was observed (Settings > Active fallback, can be disabled). Daily fetch of https://www.php.net/releases/active.php for the latest release per branch (JSON data, no remote code). No data collection. All dynamic UI text is inserted with textContent / DOM APIs. To test: clone https://github.com/Haniamin90/phplens, run `node tools/demo-server.mjs`, open http://127.0.0.1:8099/ and visit each demo state; or open any site that sends X-Powered-By: PHP/x.y.z. Grant 'Access your data for all websites' after install (MV3 optional host permissions).

summary.en-US: Warns you when a website runs an unpatched or end-of-life PHP version (CVE-2026-109618). Passive: reads server headers only, never attacks.

description.en-US:
PHPLens tells you, as you browse, whether the server behind a website runs a PHP version that is unpatched against CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619 (session.upload_progress use-after-free, unauthenticated remote code execution, CVSS 9.2, exploited in the wild) or a PHP branch that no longer receives security fixes. How it works
  • Reads the response headers your browser already received (Server, X-Powered-By, cookies, CMS headers) and a few hints in the page (generator tag, .php URLs, visible PHP errors, phpinfo pages).
  • Compares the advertised version with the patched releases (8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12) and the latest release per branch, refreshed daily from php.net.
  • Never probes, never sends payloads, never tries to trigger anything. The only request it can make to a site is one HEAD request for the page you are already on, when the passive check saw no version; you can switch that off.
What you see
  • A coloured toolbar badge: red = unpatched or end-of-life, amber = behind the latest release or a distro build that may hide backported fixes, grey = PHP detected but version hidden, green = patched.
  • A popup with the evidence, the advisory, a confidence rating and advice.
  • A one-line notification and a centered in-page dialog when a site is unsafe.
  • Per-site silencing: snooze for an hour, a day, a week, or ignore for good.
Read the verdict correctly
  • A hidden version (expose_php=Off) is reported as unverified, not as safe.
  • Distribution builds (Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL) backport fixes without changing the version number, so they are shown as Caution by default.
  • Proxies and CDNs can strip or cache headers; the popup says when a result came from a cache and lowers the confidence.
After installing on Firefox: open the add-on's Permissions tab and allow "Access your data for all websites", otherwise headers cannot be observed. Privacy: no accounts, no analytics, no telemetry. Nothing about the sites you visit is sent anywhere. Policy: https://haniamin90.github.io/phplens/PRIVACY Open source (MIT): https://github.com/Haniamin90/phplens
